facts.text: The color runs in lengthwise streaks along the nails.
My toenails have dark streaks running along them too.
I have bullous pemphigoid; it's in remission, and I'm here for my routine follow-up.
I haven't taken any medicines that could be relevant to this.
No one in my family has anything like this.

findings.name: oral examination
findings.result: Regular, brownish, reticular pattern on both sides of the buccal mucosa.

findings.name: nail examination
findings.result: Multiple longitudinal pigmented bands on the fingernails and toenails.

findings.name: nail dermoscopy
findings.result: Pseudo-Hutchinson's sign, with homogeneous brownish and grayish longitudinal bands and lines with ill-defined margins on the nail plate.

findings.result: Antinuclear antibodies, cold agglutinins and cryoglobulins within normal limits.

gold.reasoning: 1. Nail melanoma — “Dermoscopy is a useful, non-invasive, diagnostic procedure that allows us to differentiate LHS pigmented lesions from nail melanoma.” 2. Medication-induced melanonychia — “Medication-induced melanonychia ... may have similar dermoscopic patterns.” 3. Ethnic-type melanonychia — “Medication-induced melanonychia or ethnic-type melanonychia may have similar dermoscopic patterns.” 4. Drug-induced mucosal pigmentation — “Drug-induced pigmentation usually occurs after months or years of chronic drug use, and tends to resolve once drugs are discontinued.” 5. Smoker’s melanosis — “Smoking can result in oral, mucosal pigmentation called smoker's melanosis ... and it is not associated with pigmentation of the nails.” 6. Physiologic (racial) pigmentation — “Physiologic (racial) pigmentation of the oral mucosa appears in Asians, Blacks, and other dark-skinned persons, resembling LHS.” 7. Addison’s disease — “Patients with Addison's disease also have low blood pressure, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, and elevated blood urea nitrogen, due to their adrenocortical insufficiency.” 8. Peutz-Jeghers syndrome — “PJS is an autosomal dominant inherited condition featuring a combination of mucocutaneous pigmentation, intestinal polyposis and, importantly, predisposition to various types of cancer.” 9. Bandler syndrome — “BS lesions present at birth ... characterized by intestinal, vascular malformation that can cause significant gastrointestinal bleeding.” 10. McCune-Albright syndrome — “MCAS includes labial and genital pigmentation but is often unilateral and does not involve the nails. The disease is also accompanied by precocious puberty in females and fibrous dysplasia.”
